verdict.reason: Verified the absence directly. `checkSurfaceScope` builds `cited` from exactly three fields — `action.reader` (read/wait), `action.target?.reader`, `action.expect?.read` (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:187) — and never inspects `action.to?.reader`, while its own docblock still claims "Three places a reader can hide" (:176-179). The new drag destination is reader-bearing (`to: target.optional()` at :565, where `target` carries a free-string `reader` at :517) and is resolved by the runner through the same `resolveTarget` path (packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:298). Its only other validation is `assertTarget(action.to, ...)` (hunt-ui-probe.mjs:163) whose `assertReader` (:77-82) checks only the namespace prefix from `UI_READER_PREFIXES` (:61), which includes every surface — so a `slides` run can name `sheet.cellCenter` as a drag destination and pass. I searched for a counterexample elsewhere and found none: `readersForSurface`/`UI_READERS_BY_SURFACE` have no other enforcement consumer (hunt-ui.mjs:168 is only a non-empty check); hunt-ui-session.mjs contains no "surface" logic at all; the runner's surface logic covers only `goto` (:265-283) and the mounted-surface assertion (:253-259); the zod schema narrows only `surface` to `z.enum([surface])` (:559) and leaves target/to `reader` a free string (:517); and hunt-ui-tool.test.mjs has no drag/`to` case. Blocking in this lane because docs/design/harness-engineering.md:3073-3078 states the enforced-surface-pin invariant as a design commitment ("The tool checks exact names at three doors"), and the change adds a fourth door without extending the check or the doc.
